messages:
frank: Opening this thread because we've seen the same three-step failure pattern in the last 6 postmortems: KV eviction burst -> token-service P95 spike -> autoscaler oscillation. We need a compact, unambiguous runbook update and owners for follow-ups.

yasmin: Good call. Can we agree a single-page 'first responder' flow and explicit escalation thresholds? The goal is <5 min to mitigation.

oliver: I can take the runbook edits. I propose splitting the doc into: Quick Triage (1-line), Mitigations (copy/paste commands), Escalation Ladder (thresholds + who to page), and Post-Incident Remediation checklist. I'll make RW-5120 and add a PR.

mika: I'll own alert/dashboard changes (add eviction + composite suppression). ETA 72h.

frank: Suggested Quick Triage one-liner to go at the top: "1) check: kv_cache_eviction_rate & token_latency_p95, 2) run quick mitigations (batch/variant), 3) notify owners, 4) escalate if thresholds hit." Short and actionable.

yasmin: Proposed escalation thresholds (playbook):
- Notice: eviction_rate > 1.5% for 3m -> notify channel #prod-ops (Slack)
- High: eviction_rate > 4% for 5m OR token_latency_p95 > 800ms -> page eng-oncall + SRE lead
- Severe: eviction_rate > 8% for 5m OR sustained autoscaler oscillation -> page infra-manager + product-incident and open emergency incident ticket

oliver: Adding exact copy/paste commands to the Mitigations section so first responders don't guess. Use these in the runbook: 
```
# quick telemetry checks
curl -fsS "https://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=kv_cache_eviction_rate[1m]" | jq .
curl -fsS "https://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=token_latency_p95" | jq .
# quick mitigation: reduce batch size on affected pool
redwoodctl deploy --pool serve-main --set batch_size=4 --note "temp-mitigation-RW-5120"
# pin routing to low-mem variant
redwoodctl route set --model payment-model --variant lowmem-v1 --note "postmortem-RW-5120"
# fallback: route a percentage of traffic to compatible cheaper model
redwoodctl route split --model payment-model --variant lowmem-v1=20 --variant fallback-compact=10 --note "fallback-RW-5120"
# safe rollback of canary
redwoodctl rollout rollback --model payment-model --to-version stable
```

mika: For alerts I'll add panels for `kv_cache_eviction_rate`, `kv_cache_hit_ratio`, `mem.available`, and `token_latency_p95`. Composite alert will require 3 consecutive 1m buckets to fire and a 10m suppression window after temporary routing changes to avoid duplicates.

frank: Important playbook note: whenever you make a temporary routing/model-pin change, annotate with `postmortem-<ticket>` and include the incident ID in the change note so telemetry can correlate and we can auto-aggregate for the postmortem.

yasmin: Action items (explicit):
- oliver: Runbook + playbook edits (ticket RW-5120)	60% complete, PR by 2026-05-01
- mika: Dashboards & composite alert	6h ETA: 72h (by 2026-04-05)
- frank: craft the owner matrix (who pins, who changes routing, who manages scaling)	due 2026-04-03
- all: ensure any temp changes include `postmortem-RW-5120` note while testing

pager-bot: PagerBot: ticket RW-5120 created and assigned to @oliver. Due date set to 2026-05-01.

oliver: I'll add the owner matrix and the one-line Quick Triage at the top of the runbook. Putting a small verification checklist for post-change telemetry (check hit ratio + eviction decrease within 10m). PR link will be posted here when ready.

mika: Once alerts land I'll post links to dashboards and the composite alert rule. I'll also add a health-check synthetic that runs a quick KV-read pattern to detect early thrash.

frank: Great. Let's treat this as a small program: get runbook and alerts done, then run a tabletop with oncall to exercise the steps. If RW-5120 hits blockers, escalate to infra-eng lead. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
